n: Continuing from chapter 7: invaders will dig up the bones of kings, officials, priests, prophets, and citizens from their tombs—an extreme dishonor in the ancient world.

f.w: they shall bring out the bones

n: Their bones will be spread out before the sun, moon, and stars they loved and worshipped—exposed to the very “gods” that couldn’t help them—and left like manure on the ground.

f.g: The sun, moon, and stars, worshipped as gods.

f.w: for dung upon the face of the earth

n: Survivors scattered in exile will wish they were dead rather than alive.

f.w: death shall be chosen rather than life

n: God asks common-sense questions: when people fall, don’t they get back up? When someone goes the wrong way, doesn’t he turn back?
So why does Jerusalem keep turning away endlessly? They cling to deceit and refuse to come back. A wordplay: “turn” and “return” (shuv) run through these verses.

f.g: Constant turning away—a play on the Hebrew shuv (turn/return).

n: God listened, but no one said what was right or repented—no one asked, “What have I done?” Everyone charges ahead like a horse plunging into battle.

f.w: as the horse rusheth into the battle

n: Even migrating birds—stork, dove, crane, swallow—know their seasons and return on time. But God’s people don’t know His ways. Nature obeys its Creator better than His people do.

f.w: the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times

f.g: The turtledove, a migratory bird—not the reptile.

n: How can you claim to be wise because you have the Lord’s law, when the scribes’ lying pens have twisted it? Having scripture isn’t the same as obeying it.

f.w: the pen of the scribes is in vain
f.g: Or “the lying pen of the scribes has made it a lie.”

n: The so-called wise will be shamed and trapped. They rejected God’s word—so what wisdom do they really have?

f.w: they have rejected the word of the LORD

n: So their wives and fields will go to others, because everyone, from least to greatest, is greedy, and prophets and priests deal falsely. (Verses 10–12 repeat 6:12–15.)

f.w: I give their wives unto others

n: Leaders dress the people’s deep wound lightly, saying “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

f.w: Peace, peace; when there is no peace

n: They aren’t ashamed of their detestable deeds and can’t even blush, so they’ll fall when God calls them to account.
God will strip them bare: no grapes on the vine, no figs on the tree, even the leaves withered. What He gave will be taken away. Jesus’s cursing of the barren fig tree echoes this.

f.w: nor figs on the fig tree

n: The people say: why are we sitting here? Let’s flee to the fortified cities and die there quietly, because God has given us poisoned water to drink for our sins.
We hoped for peace, but nothing good came; we hoped for healing, but terror came instead.

f.w: We looked for peace, but no good came

n: The snorting of enemy horses is heard from Dan in the far north; the whole land shakes at the neighing of the war stallions as they devour the land.
God will send poisonous snakes that can’t be charmed—an image of an enemy no one can bargain with or bribe.
Jeremiah speaks his grief: my sorrow is beyond healing, my heart is sick within me.

f.w: my heart is faint in me

n: Listen to the cry of my people from a faraway land: “Isn’t the Lord in Zion? Isn’t her King there?” God answers: why did they provoke Me with idols and foreign nothings?

f.w: Is not the LORD in Zion?

n: A haunting line: “The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.” The seasons for help have come and gone. Latter-day revelation uses this line as a warning against delaying repentance.

f.w: The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved

n: Jeremiah is crushed because his people are crushed. He mourns in dark clothes, and horror grips him. A prophet who feels deeply the suffering of the people he warns.

f.g: I go about in mourning (dark clothes or a darkened face).

n: “Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there?” Gilead, east of the Jordan, was famous for a healing resin. Healing is available, so why won’t the people be healed? Christians often see Christ as the true balm and physician.

f.g: A fragrant healing resin exported from Gilead.
